lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Application or project: utilities, safety devices, and shutoffs

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic utilities, safety devices, and shutoffs task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: With a trusted adult guiding a walk-through of the real home, the learner locates and writes down or sketches the location of four safety points, confirms with the adult that each is currently accessible and unobstructed, and tests one smoke or carbon-monoxide detector using its built-in test button.
safetyNotes: The learner does not operate the main water shutoff or electrical panel during this lesson; locating and identifying them is enough.
Detector testing uses only the device's built-in test button, done with the adult present.
Completing this task sheet never certifies the walk-through by itself; a guardian confirmation is required before the task counts as complete, exactly as this course's own safety policy states.

simulationAlternative.description: If a real walk-through is not possible, the learner instead studies a floor plan (their own drawn sketch or a provided sample) and marks where each of the four safety points would typically be located in a home of that layout, explaining the reasoning for each placement.

materials: adult-or-local: access to the real home with a trusted adult
learner-local: paper or a notes app to record locations
learner-local: a working smoke or carbon-monoxide detector with a test button

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l04-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Which safety point's real location most surprised you compared to your prediction, and why does knowing its exact location matter in an actual emergency?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u02-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Location accuracy: All four safety points are correctly located, recorded, and confirmed by the adult. | Detector test and response: Test result is recorded accurately, and a next step is named if the detector did not respond. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner draw a simple floor plan marking all four safety points and add a fifth point of their own choosing, such as a first-aid kit location, explaining why they added it.

duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

resources.title: utilities, safety devices, and shutoffs worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: With a trusted adult guiding a walk-through of the real home, the learner locates and writes down or sketches the location of four safety points, confirms with the adult that each is currently accessible and unobstructed, and tests one smoke or carbon-monoxide detector using its built-in test button.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact utilities, safety devices, and shutoffs decision or action.
Model move 2: Before the walk-through, predict where you think each of the four safety points is located.
Model move 3: With your adult, walk through the home and confirm the real location of each safety point, noting whether it is currently accessible and unobstructed.

Model check: Location accuracy: All four safety points are correctly located, recorded, and confirmed by the adult. | Detector test and response: Test result is recorded accurately, and a next step is named if the detector did not respond.

resources.title: utilities, safety devices, and shutoffs action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for utilities, safety devices, and shutoffs.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: utilities, safety devices, and shutoffs coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: With a trusted adult guiding a walk-through of the real home, the learner locates and writes down or sketches the location of four safety points, confirms with the adult that each is currently accessible and unobstructed, and tests one smoke or carbon-monoxide detector using its built-in test button.
Coach direction: Before the walk-through, predict where you think each of the four safety points is located.
Learner prompt: Write your best guess for the location of each of the four safety points before checking with your adult.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: utilities, safety devices, and shutoffs complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult, walk through the home and confirm the real location of each safety point, noting whether it is currently accessible and unobstructed.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I recorded the confirmed location of the main water shutoff and whether it is accessible.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I recorded the confirmed location of the main electrical panel and whether it is accessible.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I recorded the confirmed location of the nearest fire extinguisher and its expiration status if visible.
Response 4 (t2-p4): I recorded the location of every smoke or carbon-monoxide detector I could find.

Equal-access rule: If a real walk-through is not possible, the learner instead studies a floor plan (their own drawn sketch or a provided sample) and marks where each of the four safety points would typically be located in a home of that layout, explaining the reasoning for each placement.

resources.title: utilities, safety devices, and shutoffs minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Which safety point's real location most surprised you compared to your prediction, and why does knowing its exact location matter in an actual emergency?

Success checks: Location accuracy: All four safety points are correctly located, recorded, and confirmed by the adult. | Detector test and response: Test result is recorded accurately, and a next step is named if the detector did not respond.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: utilities, safety devices, and shutoffs supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u02-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional utilities, safety devices, and shutoffs condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Location accuracy: All four safety points are correctly located, recorded, and confirmed by the adult. | Detector test and response: Test result is recorded accurately, and a next step is named if the detector did not respond..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u02-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u02-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Location accuracy: All four safety points are correctly located, recorded, and confirmed by the adult. | Detector test and response: Test result is recorded accurately, and a next step is named if the detector did not respond.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
